name: Summit AZ - Blog Salt-Free vs Salt-Based Softeners 2026-09-18
body:
> Blog · Summit Az · 2026-09-18

# Summary
Supporting blog B1 in the water softener cluster: "Salt-Based vs Salt-Free Water Softeners in Arizona Homes". Two files: the brief (`Summit-AZ-Blog-B1-Brief-SaltFree-2026-09-18.md`) and the draft (`Summit-AZ-Blog-B1-Draft-SaltFree-2026-09-18.md`, about 1,050 words). Per the change log it was created as a draft (post 11443) and published Sep 18, 2026 at `/blog/salt-free-vs-salt-based-water-softener-arizona/`.

# Keyword research (Search Atlas, Sep 18)
- Parent: "salt based vs salt free water softener" 720 / KD 23; "water conditioner vs water softener" 1,000 / KD 35; "do salt free water softeners work" 210 / KD 33.
- SERP check: the national term is owned by manufacturers and Reddit, but the Arizona version shows local water-treatment companies and plumbers, so the post was written Arizona-first.
- Primary: "salt free water softener arizona". Money terms ("water softener phoenix az", "mesa az") were left to the service pages.

# Content
- Hub it supports: `/blog/are-water-softeners-worth-it/` (position 8.5 in the prior 28 days). Money page: `/water-softeners/` then city softener pages.
- Explains that salt-free systems condition rather than soften, what changes in the home with each, and who each fits.
- Only outside facts: City of Mesa water quality page (12 to 22 grains per gallon by source, sodium increase with ion exchange, softened water harmful to landscaping).
- Flag raised: older Summit pages say "about 12 to 16 gpg", which differs from the current city figure.

# Decisions and status
- Published Sep 18 with BlogPosting and FAQPage schema, a Higgsfield banner and 2 contextual links from existing hub posts (per the case study log).
- B2 (softener sizing, "what size water softener do i need" 720 / KD 16) was planned but not started as of Oct 1.
